knowledge_point.title: Constructing and Solving a Dilution Model

question.:question/problem:
An aquarium initially holds $100L$ of water containing $3kg$ of dissolved minerals.
A solution containing $0.04kg/L$ of dissolved minerals is pumped into the aquarium at a rate of $8L/min$, while the completely mixed water is drained out at a rate of $12L/min$. If the amount of minerals $Q(t)$, in kilograms, in the tank $t$ minutes after pumping begins is given by
$Q(t) = α(1 - \frac{t}{25}) + β(1 - \frac{t}{25})^{3}$
where $α$ and $β$ are constants, what is the value of $α + β$?

> A scientific calculator is required to answer this question.
question.:question/worked-solution: At $t=0,$ the supplied model gives $Q(0)=\alpha(1-0/25)+\beta(1-0/25)^{3}=\alpha+\beta.$ The initial amount is $3\,\text{kg},$ so $\alpha+\beta=3.$

knowledge_point.title: Constructing and Solving a Dilution Model

question.:question/problem:
A juice-processing tank initially holds $100\,\text{L}$ of liquid containing $3\,\text{kg}$ of dissolved sugar.
A solution containing $0.04\,\text{kg/L}$ of dissolved sugar is pumped into the tank at a rate of $8\,\text{L/min},$ while the completely mixed liquid is drained out at a rate of $12\,\text{L/min}.$ If the amount of sugar $Q(t),$ in kilograms, in the tank $t$ minutes after pumping begins is given by

$$
Q(t)=\alpha \,(1-\frac{t}{25})+\beta {(1-\frac{t}{25})}^{3}
$$

where $\alpha $ and $\beta $ are constants, what is the value of $\alpha -\beta ?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $Q$ be the amount of dissolved substance in the tank at time $t,$ in minutes. The amount entering minus the amount leaving gives
$$\frac{dQ}{dt}=Q'_{\text{in}}-Q'_{\text{out}}.$$
The units of these rates are $\text{kg/min}.$

**Step 1**: Calculating the rate at which substance enters the tank.
$$\begin{aligned}Q'_{\text{in}}&=(0.04\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{L}})\cdot(8\,\frac{\text{L}}{\text{min}})\\
&=(0.04\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\cancel{\text{L}}})\cdot(8\,\frac{\cancel{\text{L}}}{\text{min}})\\&=0.32\,\text{kg/min}.\end{aligned}$$

**Step 2**: Calculating the rate at which substance exits the tank.
The volume is
$$V(t)=100+8t-12t=(100-4t)\,\text{L}.$$
The concentration is $\frac{Q}{100-4t}\,\text{kg/L}.$ Hence,
$$\begin{aligned}Q'_{\text{out}}&=(12\,\frac{\text{L}}{\text{min}})\cdot(\frac{Q}{100-4t}\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{L}})\\
&=(12\,\frac{\cancel{\text{L}}}{\text{min}})\cdot(\frac{Q}{100-4t}\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\cancel{\text{L}}})\\
&=\frac{12Q}{100-4t}\,\text{kg/min}=\frac{3Q}{25-t}\,\text{kg/min}.\end{aligned}$$

**Step 3**: Calculate the overall rate of change.
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dQ}{dt}&=Q'_{\text{in}}-Q'_{\text{out}}\\&=0.32-\frac{3Q}{25-t}.\end{aligned}$$
Thus,
$$\frac{dQ}{dt}+\frac{3}{25-t}Q=0.32.$$

**Step 4**: Integrate the equation.
This is a first-order linear equation with variable coefficients. So we find the general solution using an integrating factor:
$$\begin{aligned}I(t)&=e^{\int 3/(25-t)\,dt}\\&=e^{-3\ln|25-t|}\\&=e^{\ln (25-t)^{-3}}\\&=(25-t)^{-3}.\end{aligned}$$
Multiplying both sides by $I(t)=(25-t)^{-3}$ yields
$$\begin{aligned}(25-t)^{-3}\cdot(\frac{dQ}{dt}+\frac{3}{25-t}Q)&=(25-t)^{-3}\cdot 0.32\\
(25-t)^{-3}\frac{dQ}{dt}+3(25-t)^{-4}Q&=0.32(25-t)^{-3}\\\frac{d}{dt}(Q(25-t)^{-3})&=0.32(25-t)^{-3}.\end{aligned}$$
Now, we integrate with respect to $t:$
$$\begin{aligned}\int\frac{d}{dt}(Q(25-t)^{-3})\,dt&=\int 0.32(25-t)^{-3}\,dt\\Q(25-t)^{-3}&=0.32\cdot\frac{1}{2}(25-t)^{-2}+C\\Q(t)&=0.16(25-t)+C(25-t)^{3}.\end{aligned}$$
Note that $C$ is a constant of integration.
The initial condition is $Q(0)=3.$ Thus,
$$\begin{aligned}0.16(25-0)+C(25-0)^{3}&=3\\
4+C(25)^{3}&=3\\C(25)^{3}&=-1\\C&=- \frac{1}{15625}.\end{aligned}$$
Finally, we obtain the following expression for $Q(t):$
$$Q(t)=- \frac{4 t}{25} - \frac{\left(25 - t\right)^{3}}{15625} + 4.$$
Writing this in the supplied normalized form gives
$$Q(t)=4(1-\frac{t}{25})-1(1-\frac{t}{25})^{3}.$$
Finally, we have $\alpha=4,\beta=-1,$ and
$$\alpha-\beta=4-(-1)=5.$$
